title: The Unnamed
tagline: You have two days. It hunts on a schedule.
description:
You wake up somewhere you don't recognise. A man called Jeff finds you before it does, and he has about a minute to explain what's about to start happening — then he hands you a wooden sword and disappears into the trees.

You have two days.

Our first horror add-on. Found a bug? Tell us in Discord.

sections.title: It hunts on a schedule
sections.body:
Every hunt lasts five minutes. Between them there's ten minutes of quiet, and that quiet is worse.

It appears **behind you**, twenty-odd blocks out, and it does not approach. It stands there, and its head follows you.

Glance at it and you're fine. **Stare, and it comes.**

sections.title: It learns how you play
sections.body:
Hide underground and it starts arriving closer, and more often. Run, and it gets faster.

Old habits fade, so changing your tactics genuinely works — but the thing that nearly caught you last time will keep working on you until you do.

By the fourth hunt it stops arriving alone.

sections.title: Sanity
sections.body:
Being near it drains you. Looking at it drains you faster. Darkness during a hunt does it slowly.

Drop low enough and you get nausea, then a heartbeat you can't place, then whispers — and eventually the whispers start using **your username**.

Hit zero and it doesn't matter where you're hiding.

**Carrying a torch is your only real defence.** Light triples your recovery and keeps it further out. It also costs you the hand you'd put a weapon in, and that's the whole point.

sections.title: The Silence
sections.body:
There's one rule Elias gives you before he dies, and it's the only one that matters:

> "If you ever stop hearing the whispers — run. That means it isn't hiding anymore."

Sometimes everything goes quiet. No whispers, no heartbeat, nothing. There is no warning sound, no icon, no message — **the absence is the warning.** You have about seven seconds to notice and move.

Most people don't notice the first time.

sections.title: It can be killed
sections.body:
Iron won't do it. Diamond won't do it.

Find your way to the Nether, forge a **Netherite sword**, and the next hunt is a different thing entirely. The fog lifts, the effects stop, and it stops stalking you and simply comes — because it knows what you're carrying.

Five clean hits.

sections.title: Known limitations
sections.body:
- Voice scenes can occasionally glitch. If one does, report it in Discord — that feedback goes straight into the next build
- The intro only plays on a brand-new world

features: Five fully voiced story scenes with timed subtitles
Two characters: Jeff, who's been surviving this for eleven years, and Elias, who didn't
An escalating hunt cycle that runs indefinitely until you end it
Behaviour that adapts to how you personally play
A real final boss fight and a proper ending with credits
In-game settings menu — sneak + right-click — with per-channel volume, and debug tools for testing
requirements: Works on Windows, mobile and console
Turn on Cheats if you want the debug commands (optional)
install:
Download the `.mcaddon` and open it. Minecraft imports both packs automatically.

Create a **new world**, enable both packs, and spawn in.

**The intro only plays on a brand-new world.**
credits:
Story, direction and voices by **ironveil**.

Credits music: "Sad Sad Music" by **paulyudin** — used under the Pixabay Content License. We do not own this music; all rights remain with the author.

title: Tactical Villagers
description:
Iron golems are great, but a village of one bodyguard and forty panicking farmers has never felt like a settlement that can defend itself.

Tactical Villagers adds three tiers of armoured village defender who patrol, hold the line, and put down anything hostile that wanders too close.

**No experimental toggles. No scripts. Works out of the box.**

The CurseForge listing is pending approval — the download link appears here the moment it goes live.

sections.title: The Units
sections.body:
**Tactical Villager — the Guard.** The backbone of the militia. Olive field robe, plated vest with chest and mag pouches, utility belt and a goggled combat helmet. Carries an iron sword and charges anything hostile within 20 blocks.
30 HP · 6 damage · melee

**Tactical Ranger — the marksman.** Lighter, faster and squishier. Hooded, with a leather bandolier and a quiver of arrows on his back. Carries a bow and opens fire from 15 blocks — usually before the Guard has noticed there's a problem.
24 HP · ranged

**Tactical Commander — the officer.** A rare elite with a crimson helmet plume, brass pauldrons, gold-trimmed armour and an officer's sash. Swings an enchanted iron sword and shrugs off knockback that would send a Guard flying.
50 HP · 9 damage · elite melee

sections.title: How They Behave
sections.body:
They register as village defenders, patrol toward the nearest settlement, and respond to threats against it.

They target any hostile mob — zombies, skeletons, spiders, pillagers, witches — while ignoring cows, sheep and villagers. They leave creepers alone deliberately, so your guards won't detonate one in the village square.

Hit one and it remembers.

They open doors, path around hazards, and sound like villagers, because they are.

sections.title: Getting Them
sections.body:
Guards and Rangers spawn uncommonly on the surface in the five village biomes — plains, taiga, savanna, desert and snowy — then make their way toward the nearest village.

Commanders are rarer: roughly 1 in 16 Guards is promoted the moment it spawns, so finding one is a genuine event.

Spawn eggs for all three are in the Creative inventory.

sections.title: Known Limitations
sections.body:
- They spawn near villages, not strictly inside them. Bedrock's spawn rules can filter by biome and block but cannot target a village structure — an engine limitation, not an oversight
- The Ranger has no melee fallback. Corner it and it keeps trying to shoot
- Not tameable, hireable or tradeable. They're defenders, not companions

features: Three tiers of armoured village defender: Guard, Ranger and Commander
Patrol toward the nearest village and defend it from hostile mobs
Rare Commander elites with enchanted weapons and knockback resistance
Creeper-aware targeting, so guards won't detonate one in the village square
No experimental toggles and no scripts — works out of the box
Spawn eggs for all three units in the Creative inventory

title: The Unnamed — Skins
tagline: A companion skin pack for The Unnamed.
description: A skin pack built around the cast and creatures of The Unnamed. Early concept — nothing to show yet.

title: Karma System
tagline: The world remembers what you do.
description: An add-on where your actions carry consequences the world tracks and reacts to. Early concept — still working out what it becomes.

title: Lucky Dirt
description: Exactly what it sounds like. A lucky block add-on built entirely around the least lucky block in the game. Early concept.
